narrative_purpose: Makes the keystone cascade visible as a before/after: with the apex predator the forest is layered and lush; with it gone the released giants strip the understory bare.
subject: A side-by-side comparison of the same Pandoran forest under two ecological states. On the left, a balanced, multi-tiered rainforest bathed in vibrant bioluminescence, with a solitary apex predator silhouette perched high on a rocky outcrop watching over a healthy, moderate group of browsers. On the right, the same forest with the apex predator absent: the understory is overgrazed and churned into bare mud by an overgrown swarm of massive herbivores, with dim, stripped vegetation.
scene: A comparative diptych of a nocturnal Pandoran forest, contrasting a healthy predator-regulated ecosystem against a degraded, overbrowsed landscape lacking its keystone hunter.
camera: Matched wide three-quarter view of both panels at the same scale and angle so the difference reads instantly.
light: Left panel richer with glowing flora; right panel darker and barer, less living light, to signal the collapse.
palette: Cool teal-indigo throughout; the left lush with living-teal-green glow, the right desaturated and dimmer, a faint warm amber scar of churned earth on the right.
style: Hand-painted naturalist field plate, textured and observed, reads as a diagram through its paired composition.
detail_level: Moderate and matched across panels so the eye compares structure, not rendering.
composition: Two equal vertical halves side-by-side, sharing a continuous horizon and mountain ridge, separated by a subtle seam of deep indigo.
consistency_notes: The grazers are titanothere/sturmbeest archetypes; the apex silhouette is the thanator archetype. Keep builds consistent with fig-03 and fig-05.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no UI chrome, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares
